summary: Konstanz manages its pressured centre with paid street parking left of the Rhine. The council decided on 16 December 2025 to raise the on-street hourly fee to 3.00 euros (plus a 1.00 euro base amount, so the first hour costs 4.00 euros), with Strandbad Horn at 2.50 euros an hour; the city's May 2026 climate report says the higher hourly rate applies from May 2026, after a similar proposal failed on a 20:20 council vote on 29 April 2025. Resident permits cost 150 euros a year, and a new parking scheme with resident zones in Petershausen was due to start charging on 1 April 2026. Traffic cadets manage car park access by hand on about 60 high-load days a year, mostly shopping Saturdays, the Swiss National Day and Advent days. Since the Bahnhofplatz rebuild was finished in October 2025 the square is closed to car traffic (with exceptions) under the council's 2014 C-Konzept, and the city says the Marktstätte and Fischmarkt car parks are reached only via Konzilstraße. The council has decided in principle to remove street spaces left of the Rhine only if they are compensated elsewhere, so no significant reduction has happened. The Stadtwerke subsidiary KMG opened the Europabrücke car park (about 740 to 750 spaces, 1.00 to 1.50 euros an hour) in July 2025, with bus and, since April 2026, Wasserbus links; it was still under-used on Saturdays in late 2025. KMG is also taking over the Augustiner garage (288 spaces), which has been closed since 1 March 2026 for a refurbishment estimated at about 9 million euros and is expected to reopen around the end of 2026. The Döbele surface car park (435 spaces, 4.00 euros for the first hour) is planned to be redeveloped with a mobility house, with no date. The LAGO garage charges 3.00 euros an hour; the figures for the Altstadt garage date from January 2022. A draft Climate Mobility Plan 2035, reported in June 2026, proposes raising resident fees step by step to 600 euros a year and visitor fees to 6 euros an hour, but this is only a proposal: it faces opposition from Freie Wähler, CDU and FDP and each measure needs its own council decision. KMG operates 185 public charge points at 34 sites. Not read: Blick.ch (403 Access Denied) and the council information system (bot check) were not worked around.

items.text: On 16 December 2025 the council decided to raise the on-street parking fee in the left-of-Rhine city to 3.00 euros per hour (the 1.00 euro base amount stays), Strandbad Horn to 2.50 euros per hour (15 euros per day) and Strandbad Klausenhorn to 2.00 euros per hour (11 euros per day). The amending bylaw took effect on 17 December 2025; the city's May 2026 climate report says the higher hourly rate in the left-bank old town and at Strandbad Horn applies from May 2026. The stated aim is that car parks are the cheaper option for long stays and street spaces serve short stays, and the fees take account of VAT that the city has had to pay on car park income since 2025.
items.source_title: Langzeitparken in Parkhaeusern, kurzes Abstellen im Strassenraum - Stadt Konstanz (press release 19 Dec 2025)

items.text: The city's climate report of May 2026 says the earlier proposal to raise short-stay fees in the left-of-Rhine old town from 2.00 to 3.00 euros per hour, with the beach fees, was rejected by the council on 29 April 2025 by 20 votes to 20, and that a new proposal was approved in December 2025 (the new element being VAT on car park income). It says the hourly rate was raised in May 2026: the first hour now costs 4.00 euros including the 1.00 euro base amount, the second hour 7.00 euros and each further hour 3.00 euros more, a pattern the report marks as possible only at the Döbele. As of May 2026 the report lists a council paper for the third quarter of 2026 to evaluate the 2024 rise in resident permit fees and to decide on a further increase; its outcome is not known.
items.source_title: Klimaschutzstrategie Konstanz, M1 Parken teurer als OePNV (14th report, 05/2026)

items.text: A parking management scheme for Petershausen (1,110 public spaces, three kinds of zone: resident-only all day, resident and visitor all day, and resident and visitor by day with resident-only at night; 16 new ticket machines) follows a committee decision of 30 April 2024. The city's press release (updated 20 February 2026) said charging was due to begin on 1 April 2026. The city's May 2026 climate report says new resident parking zones were set up in Petershausen in April 2026 and gives the visitor fee as 1.00 euro per half hour, up to a maximum of two hours.
items.source_title: Parkraumkonzept Petershausen ist in Umsetzung - Stadt Konstanz (press release, updated 20 Feb 2026; announced start 1 April 2026) and Klimaschutzstrategie M1 (14th report, 05/2026)

items.text: The resident parking permit costs 150 euros per year (3-month short permit 45 euros) according to the city service portal read on 21 October 2026; day passes for residents' visitors cost 12 euros (blue, Paradies) or 17 euros (violet, old town and Laube).

Local outlet seemoz reports that the draft Climate Mobility Plan 2035, presented to the council committee in June 2026, lists extending parking management to more areas, with resident fees rising step by step to 600 euros per year and visitor fees to 6 euros per hour as one of five key projects (a proposal, not in force). The paper said Freie Waehler, CDU and FDP oppose higher parking charges and each measure still needs its own council decision.
items.source_title: Knappe Mehrheiten fuer gute Ideen - seemoz (12 June 2026)

items.text: The city's May 2026 climate report says that, because of an in-principle council decision to reduce street spaces in the left-of-Rhine public space only if they can be compensated elsewhere, no further spaces have been removed apart from 8 resident spaces on the Laube converted to carsharing and charging spaces. The measure to halve the roughly 2,700 inner-city street spaces (originally due by 2025, with a gradual halving outside the inner city by 2035) is marked as not begun. The report notes that the number of resident permits issued is about double the supply of spaces and that the 78 Stephansplatz spaces are to be lost from the end of 2026 (the city's Stephansplatz page, dated 14 September 2026, says the car park ceases from 14 September), while 82 new spaces appeared at the Döbele and the Europabrücke car park added 740.
items.source_title: Klimaschutzstrategie Konstanz, M2 Halbierung der Strassenstellplaetze (14th report, 05/2026)

items.text: The city uses manual traffic management on about 60 high-load days a year (nearly all busy shopping Saturdays, 1 August Swiss National Day, Advent days and various bridge days). Traffic cadets (Verkehrskadetten Konstanz-Hegau, commissioned since 2015) temporarily close and re-open access roads depending on how full the car parks are, which in practice usually takes five to fifteen minutes. Drivers are pointed to car parks on the right of the Rhine: Seerhein-Center, Benediktinerplatz (and the Landratsamt car park on Saturdays) and Europabrücke.
items.source_title: Verkehrsmanagement Hochlasttage - Stadt Konstanz (page dated 12 Jan 2026)

items.text: The rebuilt Bahnhofplatz with a roundabout at the LAGO was completed in October 2025, following the council's 'C-Konzept' decision of November 2014. Since then the square between Bodanstraße and Dammgasse is closed to car traffic, with exceptions for buses and cyclists, deliveries between 6 and 10 o'clock and residents with an exemption. The Marktstätte and Fischmarkt car parks are reached via Konzilstraße, and the LAGO and Augustiner garages via Bodanstraße. Before 2023 more than 8,000 vehicles and 550 buses used the square daily, up to 10,000 vehicles on high-load days. The page says a digital traffic management system is to regulate inflow to the centre in the medium term.

The city's car park pages (reached from its guidance system page, read on 21 October 2026) list these car parks (spaces; operator): Altstadt 359 (Parkhaus Laube Betriebs-GmbH & Co KG), LAGO 931 (Girlan Immobilien GmbH), Marktstätte 277 (Parkingmanagement Ostendorf UG), Fischmarkt 161 (Parkhaus Fischmarkt Konstanz GmbH), Döbele 435 (City of Konstanz), Europabrücke 745 (Stadtwerke Konstanz Mobil GmbH) and P+R Seepark 209. Individual pages carry dates between 2022 and 2026, and the guidance system's live counts currently list no figure for Augustiner (closed) or Petershausen.
items.source_title: Parkleitsystem - Stadt Konstanz (individual car park pages: LAGO, Marktstätte, Fischmarkt, Altstadt, Döbele, Europabrücke, P+R Seepark)

items.text: The LAGO car park (over 900 spaces according to the operator, 931 per the city's page; 1.90 m height limit; entry 07:00-01:30, exit around the clock) charges 3.00 euros per hour up to five hours, then 4.00 euros per further started hour, maximum 30 euros per 24 hours (operator page, undated, read on 21 October 2026).

Parkhaus Europabruecke (read on 21 October 2026): zone A (levels 0-2) 1.50 euros/hour and 18 euros/day, zones B and C 1.00 euro/hour and 14 euros/day; weekly maximum 70-90 euros; monthly permit 50 euros (Mon-Fri) or 75 euros (Mon-Sun). Barrier-free with licence-plate recognition, open 24 hours.

Parkplatz Doebele (435 spaces, run by the City of Konstanz) charges 4.00 euros for up to one hour, 7.00 for two hours and 3.00 euros per further hour, maximum 25 euros per day, 9:00-20:00 for cars (all day for motorhomes); the page is marked 'status June 2026'.

Parkhaus Europabrücke (750 car spaces per the operator; 740 per the city's climate report; 80 to 90 charge points depending on the passage) is a mobility hub with bus, bike hire and the long-distance bus station next to it. It cost about 18 million euros including land, of which 2.5 million came from the state's E-Quartiershub programme. The operator is Stadtwerke Konstanz Mobil GmbH and the barrier-free garage works by licence-plate recognition, with payment through the PRM service. The Stadtwerke page does not give an opening date; a ZfK article of 7 August 2025 and the city's climate reports say it went into operation in July 2025.
items.source_title: Das neue Parkhaus Europabruecke - Stadtwerke Konstanz (opening date from ZfK, 7 Aug 2025, and Klimaschutzbericht M3)

items.text: Tiefgarage Augustiner (288 spaces) has been closed since 1 March 2026 for a refurbishment of about 9 million euros, expected until about the end of 2026; it passed from the private operator B+B Parkhaus to the Stadtwerke group (Stadtwerke Konstanz Mobil GmbH will run it) after a council decision. It is to reopen with 288 spaces and 30 charge points; about 60 permanent-parker contracts were ended for 31 December 2025.

A page of the city (dated 20 May 2025) says pre-planning for a mobility house at the Döbele was presented to the committee on 7 May 2025: the administration, with Steimle Architekten and the Stadtwerke, worked out three variants, two pure mobility houses and a hybrid combining housing, parking and local shops. The technical and environmental committee was to decide on 27 May 2025 which to pursue; the participation competition was complete and bidder talks were planned for early September. The city's climate report says the Döbele car park is to be built over with housing and its parking moved into a mobility house of about 500 spaces. This is a plan with no date given.
items.source_title: Doebele aktuell / Doebele Mobilitaet - Stadt Konstanz

items.text: The city's climate report says the Europabrücke car park (740 spaces, 80 with charging) was still used too little on Saturdays in late 2025 because its fee carries no bus ticket. Its busiest day so far was 2 May 2026, with 790 parking events and 493 cars at the peak. The Wasserbus boat to the harbour has run since April 2026 and carried 300 to 460 passengers a day in April and 1,500 on 2 May, when the offer was free.
items.source_title: Klimaschutzstrategie Konstanz, M3 Ausbau von Park & Ride (13th and 14th reports)

items.text: Stadtwerke Konstanz Mobil operates 185 public charge points at 34 sites; 112 were commissioned in 2025 (including the Europabruecke car park), and more are planned for 2026 in the LAGO, Altstadt and Augustinerplatz car parks.
items.source_title: Klimaschutzstrategie Konstanz, M9 Ausbau der Ladeinfrastruktur (14th report, 05/2026)

gaps: Blick.ch articles on the Saturday traffic jams after the C-Konzept and Swiss shopping tourism returned 403 Access Denied (e.g. https://www.blick.ch/ausland/neues-verkehrskonzept-in-konstanz-wird-mega-flop-id21498661.html); no source on Einkaufstourismus volumes was read.

Council papers on konstanz.sitzung-online.de/public show a bot check page, so the Gemeinderat decisions were taken from city press releases, the climate report and seemoz instead; the Klimamobilitaetsplan adoption status after June 2026 is unknown.
Suedkurier and SWR were not reachable for search; konstanz-info.com/planen-buchen/anreise returned 502; the city's 'Chronik 2025' PDF returned 404.
No operator tariff pages found for Marktstaette, Fischmarkt, Parkhaus Altstadt (only a January 2022 city page) or Seerhein-Center; no utilisation statements except for Europabruecke.

Our feed lists Marktstaette with 288 spaces, but the city guidance page says 277 (the closed Tiefgarage Augustiner has 288 spaces), so a label or capacity mismatch in the feed is possible and unchecked.

Outcome of the planned third-quarter 2026 council paper on resident permit fees, and the 2024 resident fee rise, were not found; the Fahrradparkhaus citizens' vote (29 November 2026) and Seepark P+R (209 spaces, Saturday ticket = bus ticket, city page 14 Sept 2026) are only mentioned in passing.
Swiss-side parking policy (Kreuzlingen) and Seehas/rail park-and-ride sites were not researched.
Strandbad Horn / Staad ferry car park cashless and plate-recognition details (Stadtwerke news page, undated) were read but not used as an item because the publication date is unknown.
